reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) supports precipitation, growth, and mechanical degradation for CrNiFeCoMn, but the hypothesis extends these findings to a different alloy (Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3) without direct evidence, leaving a key premise unsupported.
premises: Precipitation and growth of σ phase and nitrides occur during elevated-temperature exposure (900-1300 K) in the HEA.
These secondary phases reduce mechanical properties.
The as-produced alloy already contains fine nitride and σ phase precipitates.
The σ phase preferentially forms at grain boundaries above ~950 K, leading to property degradation.
The proposed mechanism applies to the specific alloy Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
